newsitem.title: UK: Blair says UK Labour finished if pledges broken.
newsitem.headline: Blair says UK Labour finished if pledges broken.

text.p: Opposition Labour leader Tony Blair said his party would probably be finished forever if it broke election pledges on taxes and relations with the trade unions.
In an interview with Sunday's News of the World, Blair said that if Labour wins the May 1 election, it would have to face the British public again at the polls in five years time.

"If I break my promises on tax, on not raising basic and top rate tax, on trade unions and these essential things that I have said we will do, we are gone. We are probably finished forever," Blair said.
Labour has pledged not to increase basic and top rate income taxes for five years.
"I believe Labour lost the last couple of elections rather than the Tories winning," he said.
Blair insisted that Labour had completely changed its relationship with the trade unions.
"There is no going back to flying pickets, secondary action, the absence of ballots. That's all gone.
"My view of trade unions is very simple. They are a good part of a healthy democracy but they must never be confused with the government of the day," he said.

Blair defended the European Union's Social Chapter, saying he did not think it would affect Britain's small firms at all because its main piece of legislation was for Europe-wide firms to consult their workforces.
